title: Credential from a named accredited issuer
criterion: The wallet holder holds a credential of one named type issued by one named Redbelly accredited issuer, and that credential satisfies one condition. The recipe is about pinning the issuer; the worked condition is an AML/CTF check that passed.

types: AMLCTFCredential (worked example); any of the seven queryable types with allowedIssuers pinned
credential.schemaSource: github.com/redbellynetwork/receptor-schema commit 3b37c11, schemas/json/AMLCTFCredential.json (the five status fields are enums in the schema)
credential.queryableToday: AMLCTFCredential is the docs' own off-chain example (amlCheckStatus $eq passed) and on the queryable list.

issuer.whatAccreditedMeans: Vine: accredited issuers are the class of issuers that may grant network access, must meet minimum onboarding requirements (photo ID plus biometric for users; an onboarded officeholder for businesses), are listed in an on-chain registry, and receive a share of gas fees.

registry.abi: not public; no verified source on Routescan (RESEARCH.md question 15)

issuer.testnetDid: did:receptor:redbelly:testnet:31K82iKCtE6ciDc7oAr3T5EpjZb4S1EFM7c4xJaWkM2 (the docs' example issuer; which organisation it belongs to is not stated)
issuer.mainnet: no DID published; read the registry once its ABI is known, or ask Redbelly
issuer.namedIssuer: Averer is the only issuer Vine names, for business verification. Whether Averer issues AMLCTF credentials, and under which DID, is not stated (verify).

query.rule: allowedIssuers holds exactly the DIDs you have decided to trust, never ["*"]. The docs' contract example uses the wildcard and says in the same line to use trusted issuer DIDs in production.
query.shapeSource: The docs' off-chain single query is exactly this credentialSubject with circuitId credentialAtomicQuerySigV2 and id 100; the docs' on-chain example swaps the circuit for credentialAtomicQuerySigV2OnChain. Combining the two is the only change.
query.notNetworkAccess: This is different from permission.isAllowed. isAllowed says the wallet may transact at all (an access credential from an accredited issuer, self-enabled on the network contract). A recipe says what an action requires on top of that. A wallet can pass isAllowed and hold no AMLCTF credential.
query.oneConditionPerRequest: On-chain single query only. Requiring amlCheckStatus, pepStatus and sanctionsCheck all passed is three requests today, or one off-chain multi-query.

onChain.binding: Gated(verifier, 100) with verifier = Iden3VerifierAdapter(<your ZKPVerifier child>, <Surface>)
onChain.howTheCheckMaps: setZKPRequest(100, request) stores the query and its allowedIssuers on your verifier; the circuit checks the issuer's identity against that list, so a credential from any other issuer cannot produce an accepted proof. After submitZKPResponse(100, ...) the verifier answers true for (wallet, 100) and Gated.gated passes; otherwise NotEligible(wallet, 100).
onChain.changingIssuers: Adding or removing a trusted issuer means a new setZKPRequest. Proofs accepted under the old list stay recorded (see stickiness); if you drop an issuer because it went bad, move to a new request id so old proofs stop counting.
onChain.stickiness: An accepted proof stays on the contract after the credential expires or is revoked unless your contract enforces a freshness window (2.x, 3.x) or moves to a new request id (1.x).

fiveStates.NeverIssued: No AMLCTF credential, or no proof for request 100. NotEligible(wallet, 100).
fiveStates.Valid: A credential from the pinned issuer with amlCheckStatus passed, not revoked, proof accepted. Passes.
fiveStates.Expired: The credential envelope's expiration has passed (the schema has no validity field of its own; monitoringStatus inactive is a value, not an expiry). Fresh proof fails if the circuit checks expiry (verify); an old accepted proof stays. In tests: setValidUntil then vm.warp.
fiveStates.Revoked: The issuer revoked it (a check re-run and failed, say); the reverse hash service refuses a non-revocation proof; an old accepted proof stays. In tests: setStatus(wallet, 100, Revoked).
fiveStates.WrongJurisdiction: The credential's issuer is not in allowedIssuers, or amlCheckStatus is failed. No proof can exist. This is the state this recipe is about: a real credential from the wrong issuer is refused exactly like no credential. In tests: setStatus(wallet, 100, WrongJurisdiction).

leavesWallet: A proof for request 100 and its public inputs (holder identity, issuer, schema, query hash; exact signals verify), in a signed transaction.
landsOnChain: wallet address -> request 100 -> accepted, on your contract.
The stored request: the credential type, the pinned issuer DIDs, the condition. Anyone can read that wallets passing your gate hold an AML/CTF credential from issuer X with a passed status.
neverOnChain: The other four status fields, the holder's identity fields (the schema has none), the issuer's internal check results.
privacy.consequence: A passed AML check is a compliance fact about a person and is inferable from the gate. Say so in your privacy notice.
